title: Little Office of S. Stanislaus Kostka
translationNotice: English translation prepared for Sacrum Florilegium; not supplied in the source PDF.

blocks.source: ℣. Domine, labia mea aperies.
blocks.english: ℣. O Lord, Thou shalt open my lips.

blocks.source: ℟. Et os meum annuntiabit laudem tuam.
blocks.english: ℟. And my mouth shall declare Thy praise.

blocks.source: ℣. Deus, in adjutorium meum intende.
blocks.english: ℣. O God, come to my assistance.

blocks.source: ℟. Domine ad adjuvandum me festina. Gloria Patri, et Filio, et Spiritui Sancto, Sicut erat in principio, et nunc, et semper, et in saecula saeculorum. Amen.
blocks.english: ℟. O Lord, make haste to help me. Glory be to the Father, and to the Son, and to the Holy Ghost. As it was in the beginning, is now, and ever shall be, world without end. Amen.

blocks.source: Tu Lechiae victoriae Es auctor incurrentae.
blocks.english: The victory of Poland as she advances has thee for its author.
blocks.editorialNote: Earlier 1745 edition, not certification of the cited 1783 edition. The printed reading is “Tu Lechiae victoriae Es auctor incurrente”. The attached Latin is retained; prepared English follows the documented reading where it differs.
blocks.originalPreparedEnglish: Thou art the author of the victory of Poland [the printed final word incurrentae is unclear].

sourceReading.reading: Tu Lechiae victoriae Es auctor incurrente

blocks.source: ℣. Propter servum meum Jacob et Israel electum meum.
blocks.english: ℣. For the sake of Jacob My servant and Israel My chosen.

blocks.source: ℟. Ego ante te ibo; et gloriosos terrae humiliabo; portas aereas conteram, et vectes ferreos confringam.
blocks.english: ℟. I shall go before thee and humble the glorious ones of the earth; I shall break the gates of brass and shatter the bars of iron.

blocks.source: Deus, qui per Angelicas manus Beatum Stanislaum Kostkam sacro Christi corpore satiasti: concede propitius, ut a te in libro vitae descripti, semper in amore tui ejus intercessione crescamus. Per Dominum nostrum Jesum Christum, etc.
blocks.english: O God, Who through angelic hands didst nourish blessed Stanislaus Kostka with the sacred Body of Christ: graciously grant that, inscribed by Thee in the book of life, we may always grow in love of Thee through his intercession. Through our Lord Jesus Christ, etc.

blocks.source: Salve, cui dum Tartara Emissa per latebras Illuderent, huc Barbara Abegit in tenebras, Et Angelicum ferculum, Missum, mente pia panem, In pace Jesu corculum Mox debit levamen.
blocks.english: Hail, thou whom the powers of hell, issuing from hidden places, sought to mock; Barbara drove them back into darkness. And angelic food, bread sent from heaven, gave Jesus’ little heart relief from illness in that bread.
blocks.editorialNote: Earlier 1745 edition, not certification of the cited 1783 edition. The printed reading is “Missumque ab axe panem, In pane, Jesu corculum Morbi dedit levamen”. The attached Latin is retained; prepared English follows the documented reading where it differs.
blocks.originalPreparedEnglish: Hail, thou whom the powers of hell, issuing from hidden places, sought to mock; Barbara drove them back into darkness. [The printed sentence concerning angelic food, bread, and the heart’s relief is defective and awaits clarification.]

blocks.source: Salve, cui dum clini Affixa membra lecto Haerent, resurgunt illico Omni malo retecto: Cum nempe Kostkae Jesulum In lectulo locavit, Suumque Virgo servulum A morte liberavit.
blocks.english: Hail, thou whose limbs, fastened to a sickbed, immediately rose again when every evil was removed: for the Virgin placed the little Jesus in Kostka’s bed and freed her little servant from death.

blocks.source: ℣. In lectulo meo per noctes quaesivi, quem diligit anima mea.
blocks.english: ℣. Upon my bed by night I sought Him Whom my soul loves.

blocks.source: ℟. Tenebo illum, et non dimittam.
blocks.english: ℟. I shall hold Him and will not let Him go.

blocks.source: Salve, cui post redditam Maria sanitatem Haec verba fert, ut debitam Sequar sanctitatem. Vis Kostka Jesum sedibus Caelestibus videre? Ignatii fac aedibus, Signisque te tuere.
blocks.english: Hail, thou to whom Mary, after restoring thy health, speaks these words, that thou mayest follow the holiness thou owest: “Kostka, dost thou wish to see Jesus in the heavenly dwellings? See that thou art protected by the houses and standards of Ignatius.”
blocks.editorialNote: Earlier 1745 edition, not certification of the cited 1783 edition. The printed reading is “Sequere sanctitatem; Ignatii fac aedibus, Signisque te tuere”. The attached Latin is retained; prepared English follows the documented reading where it differs.
blocks.originalPreparedEnglish: Hail, thou to whom Mary, after restoring thy health, speaks these words, that thou mayest follow the holiness thou owest: “Kostka, dost thou wish to see Jesus in the heavenly dwellings? Place thyself under the protection of the houses and standards of Ignatius.”

sourceReading.reading: Sequere sanctitatem; Ignatii fac aedibus, Signisque te tuere

blocks.source: Audit fidelis servulus Matrem Dei docentem, Audit, nec ultra sedulus Differt sequi monentem: Sed purpuram pro vilibus Permutat inde pannis, Seseque vulgi risibus Exponit atque sannis.
blocks.english: The faithful little servant hears the Mother of God teaching; he hears and no longer delays diligently following her counsel. He exchanges purple for poor garments and exposes himself to the people’s laughter and mockery.

blocks.source: ℣. Auditu auris audivi te,
blocks.english: ℣. With the hearing of the ear I have heard Thee.

blocks.source: ℟. Et egressus factus sum, cum essem dives.
blocks.english: ℟. And I went forth, though I was rich.

blocks.source: Salve, cui nec lachrymae Patris fugam retardant, Nec patriae spes maximae, Assumpta vota tardant; Nam Jesu stipenditis Et usque militasti. Ignatii compendiis Dum sidera involasti.
blocks.english: Hail, thou whom neither thy father’s tears held back from flight, nor the greatest hopes of thy homeland delayed in thy chosen vows. For thou didst serve as a soldier in the pay of the little Jesus until thou didst fly to the stars by the shortcuts of Ignatius.
blocks.editorialNote: Earlier 1745 edition, not certification of the cited 1783 edition. The printed reading is “Nam Jesuli stipendiis Eo usque militasti, Ignatii compendiis”. The attached Latin is retained; prepared English follows the documented reading where it differs.
blocks.originalPreparedEnglish: Hail, thou whom neither thy father’s tears held back from flight, nor the greatest hopes of thy homeland delayed in thy chosen vows. For thou didst serve continually as a soldier of Jesus, and by the ways of Ignatius didst fly to the stars.

sourceReading.reading: Nam Jesuli stipendiis Eo usque militasti, Ignatii compendiis

blocks.source: Salve supernae patriae Tandem receptae civis: Qui sempiternae gloriae Felicitate vivis. Salve, tuumque caelitus Sic protegeis clientem: Ut sortiar divinitus, Quam quaero, habere mentem.
blocks.english: Hail, citizen at last received into the heavenly homeland, who livest in the happiness of everlasting glory. Hail, and from heaven protect this thy client, that by divine favour I may obtain the disposition I seek.
blocks.editorialNote: Earlier 1745 edition, not certification of the cited 1783 edition. The printed reading is “Sic protegas cliente”. The attached Latin is retained; prepared English follows the documented reading where it differs.

blocks.source: Haec, haec tuis honoribus Inscipta carpe vota, His te meis dum floribus, Et mente laudo tota; Nec me prius praeoccupet Aeternitatis hora, Quam corda panis recreet Caelestis, adlabora.
blocks.english: Receive these vows inscribed in thy honour, while with these flowers of mine and my whole mind I praise thee. Strive that the hour of eternity may not overtake me before the bread of heaven refreshes my heart.
blocks.editorialNote: Earlier 1745 edition, not certification of the cited 1783 edition. The printed reading is “Inscripta carpe vota”. The attached Latin is retained; prepared English follows the documented reading where it differs.

blocks.source: Hymnus ad S. Stanislaum Kostkam Salve, o caste Candor puritatis, Intemerate flos Virginitatis! Tuum dum corpus purum conservatur, Vultusque caeli luce illustratur, Lumina ista monstrant radiorum, Non cinctam mente beato peccatorum. Decuit corpus ita illustrari, Nescium noxa mortali gravari.
blocks.english: Hymn to Saint Stanislaus Kostka. Hail, chaste brightness of purity, undefiled flower of virginity! While thy pure body is preserved and thy face illumined with heavenly light, these lights of rays reveal a mind unwrapped in the cloud of sins. It was fitting that the body should be so illuminated, never knowing the burden of mortal guilt.
blocks.editorialNote: Earlier 1745 edition, not certification of the cited 1783 edition. The printed reading is “Non cinctam mentem nube peccatorum”. The attached Latin is retained; prepared English follows the documented reading where it differs.
blocks.originalPreparedEnglish: Hymn to Saint Stanislaus Kostka. Hail, chaste brightness of purity, undefiled flower of virginity! While thy pure body is preserved and thy face illumined with heavenly light, these lights of rays reveal [the printed clause about the blessed mind and sins is unintelligible]. It was fitting that the body should be so illuminated, never knowing the burden of mortal guilt.

blocks.source: ℣. Quasi flos rosarum in diebus vernis.
blocks.english: ℣. Like the flower of roses in spring days.

blocks.source: ℟. Et quasi lilium, sic fuit in transitu aquae.
blocks.english: ℟. And like a lily, so he was beside the flowing water.

blocks.source: ℣. Ora pro nobis, beatissime Kostka.
blocks.english: ℣. Pray for us, most blessed Kostka.

blocks.source: ℟. Ut digni efficiamur promissionibus Christi.
blocks.english: ℟. That we may be made worthy of the promises of Christ.

blocks.source: Oremus, Jesu virgineae castitatis Amator et Auctor, qui B. Stanislaum Kostkam immaculatam in hoc saeculo custodisti; concede propitius, ut qui ejus memoriam propter te et inter spiritualia lilia libenter pascere recolimus, ejus precibus ac meritis intactam a mundi illecebris animam, ac corpus pro tuo domicilio semper teneamus. Qui vivis et regnas in saecula saeculorum. Amen.
blocks.english: Let us pray. Jesus, Lover and Author of virginal chastity, Who didst keep blessed Stanislaus Kostka undefiled in this world: graciously grant that we, who gladly recall his memory for Thy sake and delight to feed among spiritual lilies, may through his prayers and merits always keep our soul and body untouched by the world’s enticements as Thy dwelling. Who livest and reignest for ever and ever. Amen.
blocks.editorialNote: Earlier 1745 edition, not certification of the cited 1783 edition. The printed reading is “B. Stanislaum Kostkam immaculatum”. The attached Latin is retained; prepared English follows the documented reading where it differs.

blocks.source: Oratio de B. Joanne Francisco Regis.
blocks.english: Prayer concerning blessed John Francis Regis.

blocks.source: Deus, qui ad plurimos pro salute animarum perferendos labores Beatum Joannem Franciscum, Confessorem tuum, mirabili charitate et invicta patientia decorasti; concede propitius, ut ejus exemplo instructi, et intercessionibus adjuti, aeternam gloriam assequamur. Per Dominum nostrum Jesum Christum, etc.
blocks.english: O God, Who didst adorn blessed John Francis Thy Confessor with wonderful charity and unconquered patience for enduring very many labours for the salvation of souls: graciously grant that, instructed by his example and aided by his intercessions, we may attain eternal glory. Through our Lord Jesus Christ, etc.

editorialNotes.text: Prepared English was compared visually with PDF pages 602–604. This office has no printed Lauds; none is added. Its repeated collects and the additional prayer for John Francis Regis remain as printed. Defective source constructions are visibly provisional or unresolved, so this office remains pending source reading.
